content.text:
The vendor is not fully living up to the contract as described in the records. ACME must provide stocked items within two business days and non-stocked specialty items within ten business days as commercially reasonable targets, and it must notify Lakeshore of any backorder within two business days and provide a committed ETA; if a backorder exceeds fifteen business days from order receipt, Lakeshore may source the item elsewhere and charge ACME the difference. The agreement also requires a monthly fill rate of not less than 95%, and ACME’s monthly report showed Exhibit B fill rates of 71% in July 2026 and 68% in August 2026, with Exhibit A above 98% in both months. [ref_id:8][ref_id:17][ref_id:1]

For Tower B specifically, the shortages are concentrated in specialty plumbing parts used there, and some Tower B orders have remained open for several weeks. The latest review says average days in “Awaiting Parts” for Tower B plumbing work orders remains well above other buildings. [ref_id:14][ref_id:15][ref_id:16]

What can be done: Supply Chain is already following up with Contract Administration and the ACME account team, and Facilities has been invited to the next vendor meeting. [ref_id:1][ref_id:0] Under the contract, if the fill rate stays below 95% for two consecutive months, Lakeshore may require expedited freight at ACME’s cost and demand a written corrective action plan within ten business days. For repeated failure to meet the service level in §7.1, the agreement states this constitutes a material breach, and either party may terminate for cause after sixty days’ written notice and an opportunity to cure. [ref_id:17][ref_id:4]

Operationally, after-hours P2 plumbing calls now route to General Maintenance first under SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4, and GM technicians are not licensed for flushometer or sensor valve, medical gas, or backflow repair; they may only make the area safe and then the ticket is reassigned to a plumber at the start of the next day shift. That process appears to be contributing to slower completion times, and the review of Rev 4 remains open. [ref_id:2][ref_id:20][ref_id:13]

If you want, I can turn this into a short action list for Contract Administration, Supply Chain, and Facilities Operations.

sourceData.section: September 2026 after-hours General Maintenance plumbing callbacks
sourceData.content:
Wendell Ruiz reported that overnight General Maintenance callouts for plumbing issues have continued to rise each month since April. Most are P2 Urgent calls for toilets and flush valves, mixing valves, and medical gas outlets on Tower B inpatient units. Under SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4, these calls route to the GM on-call first; GM technicians are not licensed for flushometer or sensor valve, medical gas, or backflow repair, so they make the area safe and the ticket is reassigned to a plumber at the start of the next day shift. Charge nurses have reported repeated overnight visits to the same room without repair. Charlotte Engel noted that Nursing understood from prior practice (Rev 3) that P2 plumbing calls would page the on-call plumber.

Action item AI-2026-06-04 (review effect of SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4 on after-hours plumbing response and completion times) remains **open**. The review has not started because the General Maintenance Supervisor position was covered on an interim basis in July and August. Corinne Ashby noted the review must also consider the FY26 overtime reduction target of 18%.

sourceData.content:
Nolan Achterberg reported a growing plumbing work order backlog in North Campus Tower B since March, primarily sensor flush valves, mixing valves, and medical gas outlet repairs on inpatient units, including the ICUs. Most of the aged Tower B plumbing work orders are on hold in "Awaiting Parts" status for Aqualine SV-200 solenoid modules and MedGuard MG-4 O2 outlet latch assemblies ordered from ACME Mechanical Supply. Several patient rooms have been taken out of service pending parts. Nolan noted that under the prior Great Lakes Plumbing Supply agreement these parts were pulled from the consignment cage the same day, and that Facilities was not consulted on the Exhibit B specialty item list in the ACME agreement before it was signed.

Tobias Lund (Supply Chain) stated that the ACME delays are **temporary**, attributed to a manufacturer allocation issue at Aqualine and to ACME establishing new manufacturer accounts. Supply Chain expects lead times to normalize by the end of the summer. The first ACME quarterly business review was held in May 2026; Supply Chain reported that fill rate reporting by Exhibit was not yet available from ACME at that time.

Charlotte Engel (Nursing) reported that out-of-service rooms in Tower B are affecting patient flow and ED boarding, and asked for estimated return-to-service dates for each room.

The vendor is not fully living up to the contract as described in the records. ACME must provide stocked items within two business days and non-stocked specialty items within ten business days as commercially reasonable targets, and it must notify Lakeshore of any backorder within two business days and provide a committed ETA; if a backorder exceeds fifteen business days from order receipt, Lakeshore may source the item elsewhere and charge ACME the difference. The agreement also requires a monthly fill rate of not less than 95%, and ACME’s monthly report showed Exhibit B fill rates of 71% in July 2026 and 68% in August 2026, with Exhibit A above 98% in both months. [ref_id:8][ref_id:17][ref_id:1]

For Tower B specifically, the shortages are concentrated in specialty plumbing parts used there, and some Tower B orders have remained open for several weeks. For repeated failure to meet the service level in §7.1, the agreement states this constitutes a material breach, and either party may terminate for cause after sixty days’ written notice and an opportunity to cure. [ref_id:17][ref_id:4]

Operationally, after-hours P2 plumbing calls now route to General Maintenance first under SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4, and GM technicians are not licensed for flushometer or sensor valve, medical gas, or backflow repair; they may only make the area safe and then the ticket is reassigned to a plumber at the start of the next day shift. That process appears to be contributing to slower completion times, and the review of Rev 4 remains open. [ref_id:2][ref_id:20][ref_id:13]

If you want, I can turn this into a short action list for Contract Administration, Supply Chain, and Facilities Operations.

sourceData.section: Summary of the plumbing parts vendor consolidation decision
sourceData.content: Supply Chain has completed its FY26 review of maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) suppliers. As part of the system-wide vendor consolidation initiative, Lakeshore Health will consolidate plumbing and mechanical parts purchasing under a single supplier, ACME Mechanical Supply. The new supply agreement, no. LH-SC-2026-017, takes effect February 24, 2026. The current Great Lakes Plumbing Supply agreement ends February 23, 2026, and will not be renewed.

sourceData.section: §2 Definitions used in the ACME Mechanical Supply agreement
sourceData.content:
§2.1 "Stocked Item" means any item listed in Exhibit A of this Agreement, which ACME maintains in inventory at its regional distribution center.

§2.2 "Non-Stocked Specialty Item" means any item listed in Exhibit B of this Agreement, which ACME procures from the manufacturer on a per-order basis.

§2.3 "Business Day" means Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays.

§2.4 "Fill Rate" means the percentage of order lines delivered complete within the applicable lead time stated in §4, measured monthly.

sourceData.title: Finance Memo - Cost of Inpatient Rooms Out of Service
sourceData.section: Using the room out of service cost in maintenance prioritization
sourceData.content: Facilities Operations and Supply Chain should use these figures when evaluating repair delays, parts stocking decisions, and vendor lead times. As an illustration of the method, a single ICU room held out of service for 14 calendar days while awaiting a repair part would cost approximately $67,200 in lost contribution margin (14 x $4,800). A non-ICU inpatient room out of service for the same period would cost approximately $30,100 (14 x $2,150). Decisions to reduce parts inventory or extend repair lead times should weigh these costs against the expected savings.

sourceData.section: North Campus Tower B building profile
sourceData.content: Tower B on North Campus opened in 2019 and is the main inpatient tower for Lakeshore Health. It has 12 floors and houses medical/surgical units, step-down units, and the intensive care units (Medical ICU, Surgical ICU, Cardiac ICU, and Neuro ICU). Tower B was designed to a higher infection prevention and water management standard than the older towers, and as a result it was built with specialty plumbing fixtures that differ from the rest of the Lakeshore Health building portfolio. Tower B is the only Lakeshore building where these specialty fixtures are the standard installation on every inpatient floor.

sourceData.section: End of Great Lakes consignment stock at North Campus
sourceData.content: Great Lakes Plumbing Supply currently maintains consignment inventory in the North Campus Central Plant storeroom. This consignment arrangement will end with the Great Lakes agreement on February 23, 2026, and Great Lakes will remove its inventory on that date. The ACME agreement does not include consignment or on-site stock. Supply Chain does not recommend purchasing the remaining consignment inventory, as ACME's two business day delivery for stocked items is expected to meet routine repair needs without the cost of holding inventory.

sourceData.title: Work Order Priority and Response Policy
sourceData.section: Measuring compliance with work order response and completion targets
sourceData.content: Facilities Operations reports compliance with response and completion targets monthly by priority, trade, campus, and building at the Facilities Operations monthly review. Time spent awaiting parts is included in completion time and is not excluded from compliance reporting; work orders on hold for parts must carry the "Awaiting Parts" status with vendor and expected date documented. Work orders that exceed their completion target are escalated to the trade supervisor at 100% of target and to the Director of Facilities Operations at 200% of target.

sourceData.section: Documentation requirements for after-hours facilities calls
sourceData.content: All after-hours calls must be entered in the CMMS before dispatch. The responding technician records arrival time, findings, actions taken, and whether the issue is within scope. Tickets reassigned from GM to a trade must show the reassignment as a separate action with the receiving trade and time. Utility failures affecting patient care must also be documented in the utility failure log per the Environment of Care utility management plan.

sourceData.section: June 2026 discussion of early experience with after-hours SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4
sourceData.content: Wendell Ruiz reported that General Maintenance night technicians are responding to more after-hours plumbing calls since SOP FAC-OPS-014 Revision 4 took effect on 2026-04-01. Many of these calls involve flush valves, mixing valves, or medical gas outlets that GM technicians are not licensed to repair, so the GM technician makes the area safe and the ticket waits for reassignment to a plumber at the start of day shift. Corinne Ashby noted that Rev 4 is tied to the FY26 overtime reduction target of 18% and that overtime data for April and May shows a reduction in trade callouts. The group agreed the effect of Rev 4 on plumbing completion times should be reviewed.
